text:
In a small town lived a kind and bookish girl named Belle. She loved reading more than anything in the world. Her father, a clever inventor, was her very best friend.

One winter, her father got lost in a snowstorm and took shelter in a mysterious, enchanted castle.

The castle belonged to a terrifying Beast — a creature as large as a bear, with tusks and claws, who had once been a selfish prince. A sorceress had cursed him until someone could love him truly.

The Beast imprisoned Belle's father for trespassing.

When Belle found out, she bravely offered herself in her father's place. The Beast accepted and her father was set free. Belle was frightened at first, but determined to be strong and to find goodness in this strange new world.

The enchanted castle was full of wonders — furniture that talked, candles that danced, and a library bigger than any she had ever dreamed of! The Beast gave it all to her. He was gruff at first, but Belle saw glimpses of kindness beneath his frightening form.

Every evening they had dinner together and talked for hours. Belle realized the Beast was thoughtful and gentle underneath his terrifying appearance. She began to look forward to their conversations.

And the Beast — who had never known real kindness — began to change.

When Belle's magic mirror showed her father was ill, the Beast let her go home — even knowing she might never return. "Go," he said quietly. "I want you to be happy."

His selfless love was the first act of true kindness he had ever shown.

Belle rushed back when she heard the Beast was dying of a broken heart. She knelt beside him and said, "I love you." Those three words broke the sorceress's curse in an instant!

A brilliant golden light filled the castle — and the Beast was transformed into a handsome young prince!

The whole enchanted castle came to life as its curse lifted. Belle and the Prince stood together, laughing and marveling at the miracle that love had brought.

🌟 THE END 🌟

💡 Moral: True beauty lives inside every heart — look for kindness, not appearance!
